plan.notes: Source: official Purdue University Northwest 2025-2026 Academic Catalog (Modern Campus Catalog), 'Degree Program: Computer Science, BS' — https://catalog.pnw.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=13&poid=5337&returnto=1955 — which publishes an official 8-semester Degree Map with per-term totals. True degree verified: PNW awards the Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Computer Science (College of Engineering and Sciences, Department of Computer Science). Transcription method: course rows transcribed verbatim from the catalog's Degree Map; the catalog's print view (captured 2026-03-03; the print endpoint rejects direct fetches with HTTP 403) was cross-checked against official catalog.pnw.edu crawls of the same page. Per-course credits: taken from the catalog's requirement blocks where printed (CS 10000=1 FYE; CS 12300=4 Technology; ENGL 10400/10500=3 each; COM 11400=3; MA 16300=5 Quantitative Reasoning); CS 12400=4, CS 12600=4, MA 16400=4 derived from the published Major Core 58-credit total together with Semester 2's exact 15-credit total (the three unknown courses must sum to 12; 4+4+4 also makes the full Major Core arithmetic close exactly at 58 — see scratch EVIDENCE.md); standard Purdue values MA 26100=4, MA 26500=3, STAT 34500=3, all other named CS courses=3, capstone choice=3. Range slots modeled inside published ranges: Semester 1 Natural Science with Lab at 4 cr; Semester 5 sciences at 3+3; Semester 7 as four 3-cr free electives; Semester 8 free electives as three 3-cr slots (9 cr, within the published 8-10). Term sums 17+15+16+15+15+15+15+12=120 equals the catalog's published 120-credit degree total; every term total falls inside its published range. Free-elective block totals 24 cr (within published 23-25). Catalog notes carried: Note 1 (ENGL 10800 substitution requires a Gen Ed approved writing-intensive English course); Note 2 (capstone choose-one may be taken in Semester 7 or 8); Note 3 (not all courses offered every semester). Milestone course: CS 27500 (m). Experiential Learning (e): ENGL 10500 and the capstone choice. The degree map prints no per-course prereqs, so all prereq lists are empty; no placement/assessment requirements are stated. Catalog spells the Semester 3 humanities slot 'Humanitites' (sic). Caveats: (1) PNW is a two-campus university (Hammond/Westville) — some courses are campus-specific, noted (H) in the catalog; (2) CS/Other electives beyond the required list must be MA 26400, CS 20600, or 30000-level+ MA/STAT/CS courses; (3) minimum grade C in all Major Core (including MA 16300 and CS 12300), 2.0 GPA required.
